theoryTitle: Physics of Resonance Tubes & Speed of Sound
theoryP1: A resonance tube apparatus is a vertical glass cylinder partially filled with water, where the air column length above the water is controlled by raising or lowering an external reservoir. The water surface acts as an acoustic closed boundary where air molecules cannot displace (displacement node, pressure antinode), while the open mouth acts as a pressure release surface (displacement antinode, pressure node).
theoryP2: Because the air streamlines flare outward at the mouth, sound waves reflect slightly beyond the physical top edge. This extra distance is the acoustic end correction (ΔL ≈ 0.61r). By measuring the difference between two successive resonant lengths L1 and L2, the distance is exactly half a wavelength (λ/2), allowing speed of sound v = 2f(L2 - L1) to be determined free of end-correction error.
theoryP3: A Helmholtz resonator consists of a rigid cavity of volume V with an open neck. The slug of air in the neck behaves like an oscillating mass on a spring formed by the compressible air volume in the cavity.
